ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure there are two slanted lines intersecting, forming upper and lower small triangles; the upper-left corner of the upper small triangle is labeled 58°, and the place on its right where it intersects the upper slanted side is labeled 100°; the lower-left corner of the lower small triangle is x°, and the place on its right where it intersects the lower slanted side is labeled 93°. Reasoning: In the upper small triangle, 100° is an exterior angle, so the corresponding interior angle is 180°−100°=80°. The third angle of the upper small triangle, namely the angle at the intersection of the two slanted lines, is 180°−58°−80°=42°. This 42° and the angle of the lower small triangle at the same intersection are vertical angles, so it is also 42°. In the lower small triangle, 93° is an exterior angle, so the corresponding interior angle is 180°−93°=87°. Thus the angle sum of the lower small triangle is x+42°+87°=180°, so x=51.

Then the angle at the shared crossing of the two diagonals is 180°−58°−80°=42°. This same 42° angle is vertical to the corresponding angle in the lower triangle. In the lower triangle, the labeled 93° angle on the bottom slanted side is exterior to the triangle, so the interior angle is 180°−93°=87°. Finally use the lower triangle angle sum: x+42°+87°=180°, giving x=51.
